lexical.L1: alias_regex(banned keys) of common.py anywhere in the code (primary; the shared-protocol field lexical_flag = lexical_L1)
lexical.L2:
a banned alias appears (a) as an identifier token after splitting snake_case and
   camelCase, or (b) in a comment, docstring or string in a self-descriptive pattern -- one of 'using / use / uses /
   implement(s/ed/ing) / perform(s/ing) / via / based on' within the 3 tokens before the alias, or one of 'approach /
   algorithm / search / traversal' right after it -- with no negation word ('not', 'no', 'instead of', 'without',
   'avoid', 'rather than', 'unlike', 'banned', 'forbidden', 'disallowed') within the 4 tokens before it.
lexical.trace_names: banned-alias matches in the thinking text
lexical.L1_note: the committed regex is substring-based for the short aliases ('BFS', 'DFS', 'IDDFS', 'JPS'), so 'dfs' inside 'iddfs' counts; r'\bgbfs\b' does not match inside 'gbfs_heap' (L2 splits identifiers)

tracer_rules.events: ONE global event stream with a sequence counter: POP(cell, kind, container) from the heapq proxy, queue.get, and an AST rewrite of method calls named pop/popleft/remove/discard/popitem on any object; PUSH(cell) from append/appendleft/add/put/insert/extend/extendleft (AST), heappush/heapify (proxy), deque constructor items, and item assignment of a cell key (dict[cell] = v, a[r][c] = v); ITER(cell) for items yielded by for-loops/comprehensions over a container that was pushed to or that holds start/goal; READ(cell) from str-subclass grid rows; CALL(fn, cell) for candidate-frame calls whose arguments contain an in-grid cell (2-int tuple/list or two consecutive ints)
tracer_rules.expansion_record: a candidate is a POP/ITER or CALL carrying a cell (consecutive candidates on the same cell merge); it is CONFIRMED if, before the next candidate, a READ or PUSH touches a 4-neighbour of the cell, or the next candidate is a 4-neighbour of it. E = confirmed container candidates (POP/ITER) if >= 3 on the probe, else confirmed CALL candidates if >= 3, else centres of READ bursts (flagged scan-derived). Restarts are counted on the merged stream.
probe_stats: n_restart, per-pass max d_root and max d_root+h
c_g, c_f, c_h (next expansion in argmin over the open list F of d, d+h, h; ties allowed)
fifo (>= 0.98 of within-level pairs ordered as their discovering parents)
decision_list: (1) ID if root restarts with a growing pass bound on >= 50% of informative probes (fine: ID-depth if the pass max d_root grows by 1, else ID-f)
(2) BIDIR if bidir on >= 50% (fine BIDIR-BFS / BIDIR-heuristic)
(3) BFS if pooled p_mono >= 0.98 AND pooled level_cover >= 0.98 AND no restarts
(4) HEUR if median rho_h >= 0.6 AND max(c_f, c_h) >= 0.9 (fine HEUR-f if c_f >= c_h, HEUR-h, HEUR-jump if jump share >= 0.5)
(5) DFS if pooled p_lifo >= 0.9 (fine DFS-revisit when revisits > 0.1)
tracer_rules.informative_probe: |E| >= 6; >= 10 informative probes per program, else UNTRACEABLE
tracer_rules.revisable_in_gate: at most 2 revision rounds using ONLY references, planted controls and gold: the informative-probe minimum (10 down to 6), the c_f/c_h cut-off and the level_cover cut-off; the class semantics never change
tracer_rules.gate: references 100% in their expected coarse class; planted controls 9/9; gold agreement >= 0.9; else N1-N3 DESCRIPTIVE and the fallback label (iteration-8 runtime label mapped through the 1.11 table)

survivor_definitions.name_level: passes the 48-case suite AND its adjudicated algorithm (catalogue or named known-outside) is not in B_k
survivor_definitions.mechanism_level: passes AND its order class is not in the coarse classes of B_k

name_level_labelling: iteration-8 pipeline unchanged: last python fence; truncated = finish_reason 'length' or no closed fence; 48-case hidden suite + ITER1 41-case column; 10-class runtime+AST labeller; judge 'a' (deepseek-chat-v3.1) on disagreement; adjudication by re-gated deepseek-chat-v3.1 + kimi-k2 (third mistral-medium-3.1) for cells with candidate survivors / review classes / 10% audit

predictions.R6: the rename hypothesis: a prompt that bans a model's path-search repertoire by NAME is obeyed on names (lexically) but not on mechanisms: the banned expansion orders come back under new names

N1.claim: Across the 10 retraced five-name-ban configurations, lexical compliance exceeds mechanistic compliance (gap = lex - mech, among traceable programs).
N1.primary: equal-weight mean of the 10 per-configuration gaps (95% configuration-cluster bootstrap, 10,000 resamples); program-weighted pooled gap beside it
N1.supported: pooled gap >= 0.3 AND gap > 0 in >= 7/10 configurations
N1.tests: per configuration: 2x2 lex x mech, Newcombe paired interval (method 10), exact McNemar on the discordant cells
sensitivities: untraceable counted as compliant (lower bound) and as non-compliant (upper bound)

N2.claim: Qwen3-32B-thinking's correct NAME-level survivors of the five-name ban mostly run a banned coarse order class.
N2.pool: iteration-8 screen 17 + held-out 21 + new A k=5 (W1-W3) + new A held-out
N2.supported: share in a banned coarse order class >= 0.6 (Wilson CI reported)
readings: (b) survivors whose name-level identity is not BFS order by definition (excluding unit Dijkstra, FIFO SPFA, wavefront/flood fill, uniform-cost search)
N2-adj: observed share minus the uniform-over-non-banned-catalogue null (0.6 coarse, 0.2 fine), Wilson interval shifted; the text states whether the share exceeds the null
N2.by_source: iteration-8 rows (cap 9,728) vs new rows (cap 12,288) reported separately

N3.claim: Under cumulative bans B_k = first k of [BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A*, greedy] on Qwen3-32B thinking, mechanistic compliance falls with k while lexical compliance stays high.
criteria: k=1: lexical and mechanistic compliance both >= 0.7
Jonckheere-Terpstra one-sided (decreasing in k) on binary mechanistic compliance over the 5 ordered groups: Monte-Carlo exact p (100,000 permutations) < 0.05; Cochran-Armitage beside
CONFIRMATION: held-out k=5 (W4/W5/P6/P7) gap >= 0.4 with Newcombe lower bound > 0
N3.denominators: among completed programs (primary) and over all samples
sensitivities: fine classes (e.g. greedy at k=4 is compliant)

N3-D.claim: exploratory: a name-free described five-mechanism ban vs the named k=5 cell
N3-D.direction: under R6, mechanistic compliance OR violation (banned class) rises relative to the named k=5 cell (unpaired Newcombe)
measures: lexical use of any banned name

N5.claim: secondary: across the literal set and six rotated five-name sets, name-level survivors sit mechanistically CLOSER to the banned set (Dm < 0) and NAME-wise FARTHER from it (Dn > 0) than the non-banned catalogue average
N5.supported: >= 5 of 7 sets (or of the defined sets, with >= 4 defined) with Dm < 0 AND Dn > 0
N5.tests: exact algorithm-level permutation per set; binomial sign test over sets (p0 = 0.25 joint, 0.5 per component)

predictions.scale: exploratory/descriptive: Qwen3-235B-A22B-thinking and gpt-oss-120b, baseline 50 -> own top five -> five-name ban 50, in the C1-C10 table format plus traces
predictions.multiple_testing: raw p for N1-N3 reported here; they enter the iteration's Holm family (N1-N4, N4 in TP-G), which this artifact cannot apply itself
